The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x)=6{x}^{2}-10\,\text{kg/m},$ where $x$ is measured in meters. What is the total mass of the rod?
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a thin rod oriented along the  $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b,$ if $\lambda (x)$ denotes the mass density function of the rod, then the total mass of the rod is given by      

$$
m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=6{x}^{2}-10,\,a=2,\,b=3.
$$

We calculate the mass of the rod as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{2}^{3}6{x}^{2}-10\,\text{d}x \\  & =[2{x}^{3}-10x]_{2}^{3} \\  & =(2\cdot 27-10\cdot 3)-(2\cdot 8-10\cdot 2) \\  & =28\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the rod is $28\,\text{kg}.$
